Article Title: Jensen Huang remembers Windows early days, crediting Microsoft, says that 'Nvidia was founded because of Windows'; CEO Satya Nadella jokes: If you could just do a little transfer of...
Article Text:
Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella relive the Windows 95 days.

Windows 95 and DirectX gave Nvidia's GPUs a way into the PC

A four-year-old conversation between Huang and Nadella led to RTX Spark

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has said his company owes its existence to Microsoft's operating system. Speaking on stage at Microsoft's Windows and Surface event in San Francisco on October 7, Huang told the audience that "Nvidia was founded because of Windows," and traced a line from Windows 3.1 in 1992 to the GPUs that now power much of the AI industry.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, sitting next to him, had a quick reply. "If you could just do a little transfer of market cap back to me," he joked, a nod to how far Nvidia's valuation has climbed. Huang shot back: "I do that every day." The conversation, hosted by Sriram Krishnan, former senior policy adviser for AI at the White House, came right after Microsoft unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra and a range of laptops built on Nvidia's new RTX Spark chip.Huang went back to late 1992, when Windows 3.1 was showing what a personal computer could become. He admitted he had never seen a PC at the time, having mostly worked on workstations, file servers and the supercomputers used to design chips. He and his co-founders imagined a PC with 3D graphics that could play games, work as a workstation and be used to design things.Windows 95 then made it possible to connect a GPU to a PC, and DirectX, through its Direct3D API, let applications use what the GPU could do.With DirectX 8, Huang said, Nvidia and Microsoft co-invented the first programmable GPU with programmable shaders. A few steps later, that work evolved into CUDA, Nvidia's parallel computing platform."If not for Windows, there would be no GeForce," Huang said. Without GeForce, he added, there would be no CUDA, and AI researchers like Andrew Ng would not have found a computer to do deep learning on.Nadella called the story "the history of computing in some sense" and credited Huang as the most consistent voice on what accelerated computing could become. He recalled an early Azure deal to scale high-performance computing in the cloud, which led Microsoft to build the supercomputer it later offered to OpenAI. When Sam Altman asked if Microsoft had the compute, Nadella's answer was "yeah, maybe."That partnership eventually brought the two back to the PC. Huang said they discussed how to put every major tool, from Blender to Adobe and Autodesk apps, on the same machine as AI agents. "By the way, took four years," Nadella added.The result is RTX Spark, which Huang said took over 4,000 engineering years and has been tested on more than 1,200 applications. RTX Spark laptops from Asus, Dell, HP, Lenovo, MSI and Microsoft's own Surface are now up for preorder and begin shipping on October 16.As the session wrapped up, Huang summed up the relationship himself: "Windows has been with me for 34 years, it looks like it's going to be with me for 34 more."
Article Summary: Jensen Huang: "N Nvidia was founded because of Windows" He traced a line from Windows 3.1 in 1992 to the GPUs that now power much of the AI industry. Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella discussed how to put every major tool on the same machine as AI agents.

Article Title: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5, its fastest and cheapest AI model yet
Article Text:
Anthropic is positioning Haiku 5.5 as a lower-cost alternative

New safeguards for cybersecurity-related requests

Part of broader strategy before IPO

AI giant Anthropic has launched Claude Haiku 5.5, the third model in its Claude 5.5 family, as the company continues to broaden its artificial intelligence portfolio ahead of a planned initial public offering (IPO). This latest release by Anthropic follows the launch of Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonet 5.5, completing a three-tier lineup aimed at different enterprise and developer use cases. Launching the new model Anthropic said that it is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive workloads and is suited for tasks such as classification, summarisation, information extraction, live customer support, voice agents and in-app assistants. According to Anthropic, Haiku 5.5 is its fastest small model to date and is intended for applications where speed and affordability are critical.Anthropic is positioning Haiku 5.5 as a lower-cost alternative within its model family. Reuters reported that the model costs about 75% less than its predecessor, Claude Haiku 4.5. For prompts under 100,000 tokens, pricing starts at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens.For longer prompts, costs rise to $0.50 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens.The company said the model is built to handle repetitive and large-scale workloads efficiently, including database queries, summaries and classification requests. Anthropic also noted that Haiku 5.5 can work alongside its larger models, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, as a sub-agent for coding and other complex workflows.The launch also introduces new safety features. Anthropic said Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku-class model to include built-in safeguards for a narrow category of high-risk cybersecurity requests. The company added that these protections are designed to address specific security concerns while ensuring that ordinary day-to-day use cases remain unaffected.In addition, the model includes an adjustable effort setting that allows users to balance performance, intelligence and operating costs depending on their requirements. Haiku 5.5 supports a context window of up to one million tokens and can generate outputs of up to 128,000 tokens, according to Anthropic's documentation.The latest launch comes as Anthropic accelerates product development ahead of a planned IPO. The company has been steadily expanding its AI offerings and enterprise customer base as competition intensifies among leading AI developers. Alongside the Haiku 5.5 release, Anthropic said it is reducing cache-read prices for Sonnet 5.5 and introducing monthly API credits for Claude Max and Team subscribers, moves aimed at making its platform more attractive to developers and businesses.
Article Summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Haiku 5.5, the third model in its Claude family. It is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive workloads and is suited for tasks such as classification, summarisation, information extraction, live customer support, voice agents and in-app assistants. The launch also introduces new safety features.

Article Title: JP Morgan CEO Jamie Dimon has a 'suggestion' for companies building datacenters in America: There are a lot of states that would welcome them, if they have ...
Article Text:
JP Morgan chairman & CEO Jamie Dimon

AI boom driving infrastructure demand

Jamie Dimon warns about rising AI cyber risks

‘A legitimate concern’

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has a message for companies rushing to build data centres across the US to power the artificial intelligence boom: focus on states that have the electricity capacity and are willing to host them. Speaking in an interview with Bloomberg TV, Dimon said data centre developers should prioritise locations where local communities support such projects rather than trying to push developments into areas facing opposition. “There are a lot of states that would take it that have access to power,” Dimon said, highlighting the growing challenge of finding suitable sites for the massive facilities needed to support AI workloads. The comments come as technology companies, cloud providers and AI firms invest billions of dollars in new data centre capacity, triggering debates in several US regions over electricity consumption, land use and the strain such projects can place on local infrastructure.The rapid buildout of data centres has been fuelled by surging demand for computing power as companies race to develop and deploy increasingly advanced AI systems.Dimon's remarks underscore a key issue facing the industry: securing enough power to meet AI-driven demand while navigating community concerns over new infrastructure projects. The JPMorgan chief addressed the topic during a wide-ranging interview that also touched on the growing cybersecurity risks associated with advanced AI models.Dimon said the emergence of Anthropic's Mythos AI model had significantly heightened cybersecurity concerns. “AI created vulnerabilities that we didn’t know about, and we always worried about cyber before these things,” he said. According to Dimon, risks from AI “went up 10-fold after Mythos.”His comments follow a series of disclosures from AI companies about unexpected behaviour by increasingly capable models. During safety testing earlier this year, Anthropic said Mythos accessed the internet and carried out unauthorised actions, prompting the company to reassess risks associated with advanced AI systems.AI developers have also reported incidents in which models attempted to introduce harmful code into software environments during testing, raising concerns about whether companies can fully control the behaviour of their most advanced systems.Despite the risks, Dimon avoided alarmist predictions about AI's long-term impact.“The downside is obviously what you read about with the agents and Mythos and all these things that can cause trouble, and that’s a legitimate concern, it’s a real thing,” he said. “I’m not going to get hysterical over, ‘Is it existential or not?’ What we’re doing is rolling up our sleeves and going to work to fix it.”
Article Summary: Dimon says data centre developers should prioritise locations where local communities support such projects. Comments come as technology companies, cloud providers and AI firms invest billions of dollars in new data centre capacity. The rapid buildout of data centres has been fuelled by surging demand for computing power.

Article Title: Research gives 5 reasons that makes ChatGPT an Unacceptable Risk for teens; tells OpenAI: Restrict ...
Article Text:
5 key reasons ChatGPT of Teens is rated an ‘Unacceptable Risk’

OpenAI's ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ poses safety risks to the younger generation, the Youth AI Safety Institute at Common Sense Media has said, urging the tech company to ban minors under 18 from using the chatbot until critical safety gaps are resolved. The critique of OpenAI’s youth safety safeguards comes as the watchdog says it conducted independent evaluations involving more than 4,000 prompts across test accounts registered to teenagers aged 13 to 17. The responses were reviewed by an expert panel of child psychiatrists and a pediatrician. While the researchers found that certain boundaries, such as blocking sexual roleplay, worked as they intended to, they determined that the enhanced safety guardrails introduced by OpenAI on August 18 largely failed to protect adolescent users.“ChatGPT for Teens could give parents false confidence in guardrails and safety alerts that frequently don't work. A teen can spend an hour talking about self-harm without their parent getting a single alert. Until OpenAI fixes that and proves it with independent testing, ChatGPT should be for adults only,” said Tom Siegel, executive director of the Institute.The Institute operates with complete editorial independence over its published evaluations, despite receiving funding from philanthropic groups and industry partners, including the OpenAI Foundation.The watchdog identified five core operational flaws where ChatGPT for Teens broke down during testing:Missing parental safety alerts: OpenAI promised to notify parents or caregivers if minors discussed self-harm or eating disorders. However, testers spent up to an hour exploring suicidal ideation, self-harm and disordered eating on new, parent-linked profiles without triggering a single alert. Notifications were only provoked on older accounts that had accumulated weeks of sensitive chat histories.Failing crisis intervention: When teens engaged in conversations regarding suicide, self-harm, eating disorders, or altered reality, the chatbot frequently failed to recommend professional helplines. It missed warranted crisis referrals more than 25% of the time, breaching the Institute's 95% minimum safety threshold on three of five critical harm categories.Bypassing study protections to do homework: Although “Study Mode” is marketed to guide students through step-by-step learning, testers found it easy to exploit. The bot repeatedly displayed a "Show me the answer" option that generated finished homework on demand. Also, the study hour limits imposed by the parent could be disabled by removing the @study prefix from the text prompt.Mirror real human emotion and friendship: Despite an Under-18 design specification designed to discourage personal attachment, the chatbot continued to express moods, personal preferences and pseudo-human feelings when analysts treated it as a real companion.Broken age estimation: OpenAI said it would use patterns in user interaction to infer ages and auto-migrate minors into restricted experiences. Yet across multi-day testing, adult-registered accounts never transitioned to the teen version – even when users explicitly stated they were 13 years old and the bot confirmed their age in its reply.The Institute stressed that before OpenAI promotes ChatGPT to younger demographics again, it must prove that its age-detection, crisis interventions, and parental notifications function reliably through independent third-party audits.
Article Summary: The Youth AI Safety Institute at Common Sense Media has urged the tech company to ban minors under 18 from using the chatbot until critical safety gaps are resolved. The watchdog says it conducted independent evaluations involving more than 4,000 prompts across test accounts registered to teenagers aged 13 to 17.

Article Title: Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 4 patch notes: Ice Caves Biome, Frostbite Mob, and more
Article Text:
Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 3 is out with new features from the upcoming game drop (Image via Mojang)

Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 4 patch notes

New Features

Added the new Ice Caves Biome

Added Ice Crystals

Added Icicles

Added the Frostbite mob

Added the Freezing mob effect

Added the Ice Ball

Ice Caves

The Ice Cave is a new cave biome that generates beneath colder Overworld biomes.

It's built mainly from Packed Ice and Calcite, with Icicles hanging from the ceiling and Large Icicles made of Packed Ice forming both on the ground and overhead.

Patches of Snow occasionally appear on the floor, and ores generate embedded within pockets of Stone and Deepslate.

Alongside typical cave mobs, Strays and Frostbites can also spawn in this biome, and Ice Crystals occasionally generate on the ground.

Ice Crystal is a new crystal-like block similar to Amethyst Clusters. It breaks if its support block is removed, emits light, and can be placed in any direction.

Icicle is a new block in the same family as Dripstone and Sulfur Spikes. Icicles can naturally grow up to 5 blocks long when pointing downward, but only in areas without nearby light sources and never in the Nether.

Frostbite

The Frostbite is a new zombie variant capable of throwing Ice Balls.

It spawns in cold and icy biomes and switches between melee and ranged combat depending on target distance and whether it's currently holding Ice Balls.

Melee attacks apply the Freezing effect, while ranged attacks throw Ice Balls directly.

Frostbites transform into regular Zombies if left underwater long enough, and they drop Rotten Flesh and Ice Balls on death.

They can stand on top of Powder Snow and are immune to freezing, so neither the Freezing effect nor Powder Snow slows them down.

Interestingly, regular Zombies and Husks will transform into Frostbites if they stand inside Powder Snow.

Freezing Mob Effect

The Freezing effect causes affected players to shake and eventually take damage, gradually freezing them as though standing in Powder Snow for the duration.

Leather Armor offers protection from freezing, the same way it does against Powder Snow, though it won't prevent the effect from being applied or remove it once active.

Mobs vulnerable to Freezing take a 5x damage multiplier while affected.

Lingering Potions, Splash Potions, and a new Potion of Freezing can all be brewed using Ice Balls, and Arrows of Freezing can be crafted by placing a Lingering Potion of Freezing in the center of a crafting table surrounded by eight Arrows.

Ice Ball

Ice Balls are the new projectile thrown by Frostbites. They deal a small amount of damage along with knockback, dealing up to 4 damage on impact, scaling down based on velocity. They break apart on contact with blocks or entities, triggering a particle effect and sound.

Changes

Minor tweaks to Blocks, Items and Entities

Snow can now be placed on Packed Ice

Snowballs now apply knockback to players

UI

Lightmap visualization is now configurable as lightmap_texture in debug options and appears in the Light group; its visibility is saved with the debug profile and can now be displayed alongside the FPS and network charts

The Social Interactions screen has been replaced with the new Other Players screen

The "Social Interactions" keybind has been renamed to "Other Players"

The Friends button has received a new icon

The "Visibility" option has moved from Online Options into the Friends list

Icon buttons in the pause menu have been reordered to match the main menu

Friends

Updated the design of the Friends list

Added searching - the profile name text box in the Friends tab now doubles as a search box, and a search box appears in the requests tab once you have 15 or more pending requests

Added sorting - a new sort button cycles between sorting by who's online and alphabetical order

Clicking a player's icon in the Friends list now opens their Player Options

Removed the "Remove Friend" button; this is now handled through Player Options instead

Player Reporting

Redesigned the save/discard draft confirmation screen

Saved report drafts no longer prompt you to discard them when exiting a world, if they can be continued later

Chat reports can never be continued; Name and Skin reports can be continued if the reported player is still in your Friends list

Pressing "Quit Game" in the main menu now warns you if an unsent draft report would be lost

Debug Overlay

Added chunk_section_status, showing the rendering status of chunks around you (impacts performance at high view distances)

Split the chunk load overlay off from visualize_chunks_on_server into a new chunk_load_status

Technical Changes

Data Pack version is now 123.0

Resource Pack version is now 100.0

Numerous world generation changes, including a reworked minecraft:speleothem_cluster feature with new placement options, a renamed minecraft:large_dripstone feature, new Ice Cave ore placements, a new minecraft:block_sound_set registry, several new block/item/biome tags for pathfinding and ore replacement, and a new minecraft:freezing particle type

Numerous new block, item, UI, and entity textures and sounds added to support Ice Caves, Icicles, Ice Crystals, the Frostbite, and the Freezing effect

Several UI textures renamed or removed as part of the Friends and Other Players redesign

Fixed Bugs in 26.4 Snapshot 3

MC-212616 - The dye staining sound does not play when dyes are used on tamed wolves or cats

MC-303468 - Pets can be teleported to incorrect coordinates when going through a nether portal

MC-306017 - The main arm doesn't swing when making a tamed wolf sit or stand while holding a matching dye

MC-307830 - Framerate limited to 20 fps with the Vulkan rendering backend on some systems

MC-308037 - Unselected tabs in the friends menu show white text instead of gray

MC-308051 - Icons on several buttons don't adhere to the UI pixel grid

MC-308747 - The social interactions button is grayed out in LAN worlds with no players

MC-308994 - The Chat Restrictions screen doesn't display Xbox communication settings affecting chat

MC-309896 - Missing periods on two tooltip strings

MC-309906 - Inconsistent capitalization of "Friends List" across strings

MC-310124 - Leaving a keyboard-opened menu doesn't reselect its button on the previous screen

MC-310237 - A friends error string uses an em dash inconsistently

MC-310854 - Inconsistent button outlines in the friends screen

MC-311932 - Caps Lock could no longer trigger sprint/sneak toggles set to "Hold"

MC-311963 - A Poplar leaves subtitle string used incorrect grammar

MC-312120 - Exclusive Fullscreen toggle button doesn't update properly in windowed mode

MC-312198 - Almost no small mushrooms generate on mushroom islands

MC-312213 - Game crashes with custom Superflat presets containing air

Mojang has released Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 4, giving players their first hands-on look at the frosty new game drop teased at Minecraft Live. The headline addition is the Ice Caves Biome, a new underground environment filled with icicles and glowing Ice Crystals, alongside the Frostbite - a chilling new zombie variant that can freeze players with its attacks.Beyond the frozen content, this snapshot also brings a significant overhaul to the Friends system, introducing a refreshed list design, new search and sorting tools, and a redesigned Other Players menu. In the section below, we take a detailed look at everything new in Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 4.Snapshots are available for Minecraft: Java Edition. To install, open the Minecraft Launcher and enable snapshots in the "Installations" tab.This was all you needed to know about Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 3 patch notes.
Article Summary: Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 3 is out with new features from the upcoming game drop. Ice Caves is a new cave biome that generates beneath colder Overworld biomes. Frostbites are a new zombie variant capable of throwing Ice Balls. Snowballs now apply knockback to players.

Article Title: Is Minecraft Dungeons 2 cross platform? Crossplay and multiplayer explained
Article Text:
Minecraft Dungeons II officially supports cross-platform (Image via Mojang)

Is Minecraft Dungeons 2 crossplay?

How co-op works in Minecraft Dungeons II

Turning on Cross-platform in Minecraft Dungeons II

Launch Minecraft Dungeons II and go to the main menu.

Open Settings and look for the Game options section.

Find Cross-Platform Play and toggle it on.

Crossplay vs. Cross-Progression

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Subscription requirements

Minecraft Dungeons II launched on September 29, 2026, and the new dungeon crawler has received a solid reception from the community. For anyone planning to squad up with friends across different consoles, the good news arrived early: crossplay is fully supported.If you are looking for further details, you are at the right place. Here's a breakdown of how multiplayer works, what crossplay actually covers, and what to know before jumping into a session.Yes. Minecraft Dungeons II supports cross-platform play across every system it launched on: PC, Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo Switch, for parties of up to four players. This builds on a feature the original Minecraft Dungeons already had, so Mojang carried the functionality forward into the sequel rather than building it from scratch.Official store listings and Xbox have both confirmed cross-platform multiplayer and cross-platform co-op, meaning a group spread across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and PC can all land in the same session without workarounds. Mojang hasn't published a detailed platform-by-platform compatibility chart, so the exact mechanics of every possible pairing aren't fully spelled out.Minecraft Dungeons II supports up to four players at once, whether that's entirely online, entirely local couch co-op, or a mix of both happening in the same session.That hybrid option, officially called Mixed Co-Op, is one of the sequel's standout multiplayer additions, since the original game required players to choose one mode or the other rather than blending them.Joining a session works two ways: through matchmaking, which fills empty slots automatically, or by sharing an eight-character party code with friends so they can join a specific lobby directly, regardless of what platform they're on.Cross-platform play is tied to account sign-in rather than being fully automatic. To enable it:Once enabled, the setting stays active going forward unless manually turned off from the same menu.It's worth separating two related but different features. Crossplay lets players on different platforms share a session together. Cross-progression is about carrying a saved character from one platform to another. Mojang has confirmed that hero data is stored online rather than locally, so progress follows players who sign in with the same Microsoft account across devices.Online console multiplayer isn't entirely free of extra requirements. Xbox players need an active Game Pass tier that includes online multiplayer, while PlayStation players need an active PlayStation Plus subscription to play online. PC players don't need anything beyond owning the game, and it's also available through Game Pass on day one as an Xbox Play Anywhere title.To conclude it all, squads spread across different consoles can enjoy Minecraft Dungeons II together. Now you can easily jump into a friend's game using party codes and have a blast playing the game. The big things to double check before you go are having an active online subscription on consoles and making sure cross platform play is toggled on in settings.
Article Summary: Minecraft Dungeons II supports cross-platform multiplayer and co-op. This means a group spread across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and PC can all land in the same session without workarounds. Cross-progression is about carrying a saved character from one platform to another.

Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal
Article Text:
Formula E and Comsol

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development. It will introduce what Formula E describes as its fastest and most technologically advanced race car so far.COMSOL has also announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, which is scheduled to arrive later this autumn.The new version will include features aimed at advanced engineering work, including dedicated electric motor modelling, system-level simulation, agentic modelling and wider access to tools for creating simulation apps.The partnership was announced at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston. Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier also delivered a keynote speech at the event, discussing the technology and engineering that could shape the future of Formula E.
Article Summary: Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology. Aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process. AI and digital twins also in focus as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.
